title: Building verification loops in Claude Code
format_note: Presenter-led how-to: on-camera talk cut with typographic cards, a loop diagram and real app screen recordings; no music, no logo end card.
one_thing: Checks you do by hand can be codified so Claude verifies its own work in a loop.

transcript.voice_style: Calm, conversational, unhurried; steady explanatory pace with pauses at most cuts; no hype or sales language.
transcript.script_shape: Loop explained, manual QA named per platform, verify skill shown, extended with a layout-shift trace, demoed on a Like button, closed by a rule of thumb.

structure.frame0: Presenter at a desk in a warm room with a lower-third 'Delba de Oliveira / Claude Code'; subject and speaker are present at t=0, not black or logo.
structure.first_3s: Talking head speaks the first line, then at 2.58 a short dissolve to a cream card with one 'Prompt' box that starts the loop diagram.

beats.what: Presenter opens: 'For every prompt you send, Claude Code runs a loop', lower-third naming her.
Diagram builds box by box: Prompt, Gather context, Take action, Verify results, with a return arrow.
Presenter and real browser and chat screens show the verify step being you clicking around the page.
Card 'Hand off your manual checks' then 'Verifying a change': grid of tests, type checks, linters turns green.
Manual QA table adds Web app, Back end, Mobile app rows, voice says passing checks does not prove intent.
iOS Simulator inside the app window: quantity 2 yet total $4.50, Claude edits, total $9.00.
'Codify your checks', then /verify creates SKILL.md; presenter interleaves; a step is added to the skill; 'The verification loop' card.
One 42.5 s screen shot: Like button task, CLS 0.19 found, banner fix, CLS 0.00, cursor tracks the summary.
Presenter then cards 'When Claude can verify its own work' with three lines and 'What to codify next' with three examples.
Presenter closes on camera with the rule of thumb; no logo or URL card.

hero_moment.what: Chat shows 'CLS went from 0.19 to 0.00' and the verified summary; the failing-then-passing check is the proof the film exists to show.

ending.what: Last 5.2 s is the presenter speaking to camera after the 'What to codify next' card; no logo, URL or end card.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Alternates presenter shots of 2-13 s with cream or tan cards; cuts at 8.64 a minute with no burst; one 42.5 s screen shot (22.7% of runtime) carries the demo; card lists build a row per spoken item.

look.ground: Warm cream (#F5F4ED-like) and tan cards for graphics; screen recordings sit in a window on a mid blue ground; presenter shot is warm and dark.
look.accent_use: Terracotta only for the product's own UI (ACME COFFEE label, Liked pill, spinner); sage, pink and blue tint boxes encode pass, fail and verify.
look.type: High-contrast serif for card titles and the lower-third name; grotesque sans for lists and UI; titles sit left-aligned at an indented margin, list rows in two columns.
look.depth: Flat: cards are plain colour with no shadow or texture; the only depth is the app window floating on the blue ground and the phone bezel.

product_ui.camera_on_ui: Screen shots are static crops of the app window with scrolling text; a cropped-in browser view at t=12 and the simulator at t=58; no zoom or pan moves.
product_ui.notes: Chat text is about 17 px tall on a 720 px frame and code lines smaller, so only the bold result lines read at phone width. Key lines like 'CLS went from 0.19 to 0.00' are small; the film relies on voice to carry them.

motion.text_entry: Card titles fade in softly with a brief blur; list rows are added one at a time and held; exits fade word by word left to right in about 0.35 s (strips/window-14-20.5s.jpg).
motion.ui_motion: Chat messages type in, tool rows stack, old lines fade to grey as new ones arrive, and the spinner runs; a real cursor moves over the result text in the long shot.
motion.camera: No camera moves on cards or UI; the presenter shot is locked off and the only movement is hand gesture.
motion.eases: Soft opacity fades; arrow and box appear in sequence in the diagram (strips/window-03-5.709s.jpg); no bounce or overshoot seen.

transitions.cause: Presenter to card, a one-to-two frame dissolve as she finishes a sentence.
Text fades out on tan, card changes to cream and next title blurs in.
Typed text in the chat box changes the UI; slash menu opens.
Presenter picks up after screen demo.
Blurred app window sharpens into place after the card.

on_screen_lines.text: Web app: Open the page, click around, watch the console
Back end: Call an endpoint, read the response
Mobile app: Tap through the screens in a simulator
When Claude can verify its own work
It gets further on its own
It takes fewer rounds of back and forth

copy.holds_vs_reading_rule: Card lines hold far longer than 0.5 s + 0.3 s a word because they trail the voice; the last list line holds about 1.8 s, under the 2 s floor.

sound.music: No music evidenced: describe tags give speech 0.916 and music 0.105, below the 0.2 floor, and there is no steady beat (bpm null).
sound.sfx: No sfx evidenced; describe tags show only click 0.113 and writing 0.155, both below 0.2.
sound.vo_music_balance: Voice only; integrated loudness -23.9 LUFS, short-term max -21.2, true peak -4.6 dBTP, loudness range 3.5 LU.
sound.energy_arc: Flat and conversational throughout; strong onsets about 20.5 a minute come from speech; silence gaps of 0.3-1 s fall near most cuts.
sound.sync_to_picture: cuts_on_strong_onset_share 0.111 against chance 0.077 is a 0.034 gap, so cuts are not locked to the sound; they follow sentence ends in the speech.

good.observation: The diagram builds one box per spoken phrase, so voice and picture state the same loop; the return arrow lands as the verify step is named.
The proof is shown as a failing then passing state in real UI: total $4.50 with quantity 2, then $9.00 after the fix.
Card lists add one row per spoken item and keep earlier rows, so the viewer reads along and the full list is on screen at the end.
A single long uncut screen shot of 42.5 s carries the demo, with greyed-out old lines and a cursor showing where to read.
Restrained palette and a single serif and sans pairing make the cards and the product windows feel like one house style.
Presenter returns at sentence ends, so the human voice frames each card, with a lower-third on frame 0.

weak.observation: Chat and code text in screen shots is small; at phone width only the bold result lines would read.
Loudness is -23.9 LUFS with a -4.6 dBTP peak, well below a social master's -14 LUFS.
No end card, URL or logo; the film ends on the presenter's last sentence.
'When Claude can verify its own work' runs 7 words on a line and the last list line holds under 2 s.

rule_candidates.rule: When a spoken list has three parts, show a card that adds one row per item and leaves earlier rows on screen until the card ends.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0020.jpg, f0022 sequence 40-48 s; Manual QA rows at 39, 42, 45 s

rule_candidates.rule: Show a verify step as a fail state then a pass state in the same real UI with one changed number.
rule_candidates.evidence: $4.50 with quantity 2 at 58 s (sheet-02.jpg), $9.00 at 60 s (f0031.jpg); CLS 0.19 to 0.00

rule_candidates.rule: A tutorial may cut every 4.8 s median, not 1.8-3.5 s, when voice carries the content and shots change at sentence ends.
Brief 1-2 frame dissolves are tolerable between a presenter and a card when voice continues across them.
Fade card text out word by word left to right in about 0.35 s; exits shorter than the 0.5 s title entrance.
Voice-only tutorials need no music, but loudness should still reach -14 LUFS for social; this film sits at -23.9.
Open a presenter film on frame 0 with the speaker and a lower-third name, then reach the first graphic within 3 s.
Keep card titles to 5-9 % of frame height with at most 6 words; a 7-word line read at 5.4 % feels long.
